items.headline: DEA restarts 7-OH scheduling with a 1 mg-per-gram threshold aimed at enhanced kratom products
items.summary: DEA published a new notice of intent to temporarily place 7-hydroxymitragynine and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl in Schedule I above 1 mg per gram in solids or 1 mg per milliliter in liquids, or when the mitragynine ratio falls below 100 to 1, withdrawing its July notice that used a lower threshold. The order can be published on or after November 13 and would last two years, leaving botanical kratom below the line uncovered. Concentrated 7-OH products remain on shelves until then, so screening for 7-OH use and withdrawal stays important.

items.headline: Medetomidine in fentanyl supply drives sharp rise in ICU dexmedetomidine use for OUD admissions
items.summary: HealthDay reports that a JAMA Internal Medicine research letter (published Sept. 28) covering 11,846 OUD-related admissions at two Philadelphia hospitals found dexmedetomidine was given in 5.8% of admissions from 2020 to early 2024 but in 19.8% once medetomidine entered the local fentanyl supply, reaching 31.7% by the third quarter of 2025. Nearly all admissions involving dexmedetomidine (99.5%) required the ICU, with longer ICU stays and more discharges before medically advised (27.8% vs 16.6%). The findings signal that hospitals in regions seeing medetomidine need withdrawal protocols, ICU capacity planning, and robust methadone and buprenorphine access.

items.headline: Nearly half of people taking GLP-1 drugs report drinking less alcohol after starting
items.summary: In a nationally representative survey of more than 2,000 U.S. adults, 106 of 242 respondents who had used a GLP-1 receptor agonist (44.2%) reported drinking less alcohol after starting treatment. Among those who screened positive for potentially unhealthy alcohol use, 71 of 129 (54.1%) reported cutting back. The self-reported data add real-world support to early trials suggesting GLP-1 drugs may reduce drinking, and offer clinicians a reason to ask about alcohol use when these medications are started.

items.headline: States with more AUD among women often have fewer women-specific treatment services
items.outlet: Boston University School of Public Health
items.summary: A study in Substance Use & Addiction Journal estimated alcohol use disorder among women ranged from 6.2% in Utah to 12.7% in Washington, DC, against a national average of 8%. Of nearly 14,000 adult alcohol treatment facilities, only 58.5% offered women-specific programming and just 4.6% provided childcare, with many high-prevalence states below average. The authors urge states to incentivize childcare and telehealth, require coverage of all FDA-approved AUD medications, and expand AUD screening in primary care.

items.headline: Pennsylvania Supreme Court rejects co-user defense in drug delivery resulting in death cases
items.summary: Pennsylvania's highest court upheld two York County convictions, ruling that state law's broad definition of delivery does not distinguish drug dealers from people who jointly acquire and use drugs, while noting the policy question belongs to the General Assembly. Drug delivery resulting in death charges, which carry up to 40 years in prison, were filed more than 680 times from 2021 through 2025. Critics warn the ruling may further discourage people from calling for help during an overdose, a concern for harm-reduction and Good Samaritan efforts.
